notes.summary: The genuine singular mixed E1 operator, exact mass and energy, target criterion, comparison and uniqueness are available in BJ. Arbitrary-support existence remains equivalent to, and conditional on, genuine envelopes.
notes.detailedSummary: Reconstructed from BJ1801.08229v4 in its reduced irreducible projective, possibly nonnormal scope over algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero fields, for every ample line bundle and ample real numerical Cartier class. Relative integral closure retains the generic fiber. The model/intersection operator has raw mass V, probability normalization and E(phi+c)=E(phi)+c. All-E1 integrability is equivalent to finite dual energy, but sufficiency for solvability requires EP. The actual general-variety equation equivalence, compactness, derivative, attainment and completeness are kept distinct from the smooth sufficient envelope theorem.
notes.text:
Primary-source partial theorem. Let k be algebraically closed, trivially valued and characteristic zero, X reduced irreducible projective of dimension n, and omega an ample real numerical Cartier class, including c1(L) for every ample line bundle. Set V=(omega^n)>0. BJ1801.08229v4 expressly permits nonnormal varieties in its conventions, returns to general varieties in Section 7, and assumes irreducibility rather than smoothness in Theorem 12.8. The sufficient envelope theorem 5.20 assumes smoothness and connectedness, and in our domain characteristic zero. It is not an unconditional singular theorem.

Test configurations are integrally closed in their prescribed generic fiber. Absolute normalization would change a nonnormal X. BJ1.13 gives vertical DVRs. For a central component E write b_E=ord_E(t) and v_E=b_E^(-1)ord_E. On a common configuration, the genuine mixed raw model measure is sum_E b_E product_i((omega_i,model+D_i)|E) delta_vE. Relatively nef classes give nonnegative weights, and the central-fiber cycle gives mass (omega_1...omega_n). These are actual intersection measures.

The compactified intersection pairing extends by decreasing model majorants, is finite on mixed finite-energy tuples, and extends multilinearly to differences. BJ7.18 defines its Radon measure by integral h M=pairing((0,h),(omega_1,phi_1),...,(omega_n,phi_n)) for genuine model-PL tests. Positivity bounds this functional by its mass times the sup norm; PL density and Radon representation give existence and uniqueness. BJ7.19 proves model agreement, exact mass, mixed integrability, decreasing continuity and normalization pushforward. Weighted continuity7.21 uses the pairing containing the test minus the pairing containing zero. The general operator is therefore constructed before equation surjectivity.

The actual trivial-reference energy is E(phi)=pairing((omega,phi)^(n+1))/((n+1)V), with E(0)=0 and E(phi+c)=E(phi)+c. E1 consists of genuine global psh potentials with E>−infinity. Raw diagonal MA has mass V; probability MA=raw/V. Locality for maxima has the measure of the winning potential on its strict winning locus. Equal masses give integral_{phi<psi} MA(psi)<=integral_{phi<psi} MA(phi). With I=integral (phi-psi)(MA(psi)-MA(phi)), mixed estimates give I>=0. Equal measures imply I=0; finite-dual-energy divisorial Dirac tests and minimal usc divisorial extension give equality after equal-sup normalization. Thus uniqueness is modulo one real constant. BJ10.6 global domination also precedes EP; it applies only to genuine global potentials.

For a raw positive Radon target nu its mass is exactly V. Put mu=nu/V. The finite-dual-energy condition is sup_{psi in E1}(E(psi)-integral psi mu)<infinity. BJ9.20 proves equivalence with integrability of every E1 potential, without asserting solvability. Its bounded-J weighted-sum argument rules out unbounded target integrals: a decreasing sum of normalized psi_j with J bounded and integrals <=−2^j would have finite energy but integral −infinity. The mixed expansion I(t psi,0)<=t[1-(1-t)^n]I(psi,0)<=n t^2 I(psi,0) supplies the scaling estimate. Necessity for actual MA targets follows from the energy tangent inequality.

Under genuine EP, general BJ5.11 supplies normalized-PSH compactness. The uniform two-sided energy derivative8.5, bounded-J target L1 convergence9.19 and energy usc give variational attainment. The target approximation by maximizing model measures9.11 precedes attainment. Testing both f and −f forces the constructed genuine MA measure to equal mu. The raw objective is VE−integral phi nu, and mass V gives translation invariance. Target completeness and the MA embedding give strong E1 completeness after surjectivity. Conversely completeness of bounded increasing model maxima supplies envelopes. This is the actual general-variety EP/surjectivity equivalence12.8, not the smooth sufficient theorem12.9. The original singular equation is not proved by this conditional implication. Dimension zero is the separate constant one-point case.

notes.summary: Relative tropical supports on curves give positive outgoing slopes and radial trace equality without ambient convex extension or arbitrary-H(s) affine regularization. Determinants and actual FS tests fix slicing weights before choosing a weak witness.
notes.detailedSummary: The curve proof uses a common semistable skeleton for finite unit logs, handles zero and identically-zero coordinates, type I/IV neighborhoods and real breakpoints, and applies the actual positive-lisse-Laplacian criterion and decreasing stability. Radial equality checks a nontrivial complete algebraically closed extension, Wanner’s smooth proper scope, disk comparison, ramification, properness, Artinian dimensions and minus-infinity cases. The determinant maximum meets the exact affine FS floor/generator condition. Global FS tests fix nonflat slicing weights, permitting a line adapted to the birational witness. The preceding smooth weak open-trace extension remains an explicit antecedent.
notes.text:
Independent curve and algebra proof drafts. Correct Wu2609.27610v1's relative contact condition to f(t')>=ell(t')+C with equality at t, and retain its finite affine convention. This auxiliary correction does not redefine the genuine global PSH problem. For a smooth curve over complete algebraically closed nontrivially valued Omega of residue characteristic zero, a finite continuous PL selection in regular log-norm coordinates with these relative supports is subharmonic.

At infinite coordinates, finite affine expressions have zero coefficient on a smaller chart; identically-zero pulled coordinates are discarded. All remaining coordinates are units. Thuillier2.2.24 factors their logs through a common strictly semistable skeleton, and2.3.20 makes them harmonic. Along each subdivided edge the coordinates are affine; a continuous selection among finitely many affine functions switches only at finitely many intersections. Hence the pullback is lisse, including real breakpoints. Unit-log germs are locally constant at type I/IV points by Thuillier2.3.21. At an interior skeleton point subtract the pulled-back harmonic contact support. Every outgoing slope is nonnegative; the harmonic weighted slope sum is zero. The lisse Laplacian coefficient is therefore sum_e w_e slope_e(b−H)>=0. Wanner2.11/Thuillier3.4.4 gives subharmonicity; Thuillier3.1.8(ii) passes decreasing limits, with the identically −infinity alternative. No ambient convex extension is asserted. Relative supports on the union of rays (1,0),(0,1),(1,1), with values 0,0,t, show why such an extension is an additional statement.

For any complete residue-characteristic-zero F, extend to Omega. If F is trivial first use F((T)), |T|=e^−1, then its completed algebraic closure; otherwise use the completed algebraic closure of F. Wanner's standing field is complete, algebraically closed and nontrivially valued, and Section4 additionally fixes a smooth proper algebraic curve. When invoking4.3 or4.7, compactify the smooth curves by their normal projective function-field models and apply only on the original opens. The slope proof itself uses Section2 and Thuillier.

Disk comparison gives h(center)<=h(boundary Gauss). Usc and convergence of those Gauss points to the rational center give the reverse limiting inequality, including a −infinity center. This is a radial boundary limit, not an ordinary punctured-neighborhood limit. A finite curve map locally has t=c z^e U(z), U(0)=1. Residue characteristic zero bounds binomial coefficients and permits an analytic e-th root of U, so after an invertible coordinate change t=c y^e. A small target Gauss point has one source Gauss point per source disk, with actual fiber dimension e: after scaling, Y^e=alpha T is Eisenstein over the residue rational-function field. The center's Artinian length is also e. Finite properness excludes other preimages nearby. Radial limits prove the weighted center equality; if a summand tends to −infinity the others are locally bounded above, so no subtraction of infinities is needed.

Trace base change has a separate Artinian proof for every pulled-back function. Tensor each local fiber factor with the extended completed residue field. Refined factor dimensions sum to the original dimension, and their finite residue norms restrict to the original point. Thus the weighted trace identity needs no regularizable-function antecedent.

For reduced finite locally free B/A of rank d and actual affine FS u=max(lambda,c_i log|f_i|+C_i), clear coefficients with integer D, set b0=1, bi=f_i^(D c_i), w0=D lambda and wi=D C_i. The basis-independent determinant P(T)=det(mult_(sum T_i bi))=sum a_beta T^beta is in A[T]. Artinian composition series give P=product_x(sum T_i bi(x))^length_x after algebraically closed extension. Weighted Gauss norms are multiplicative for all positive real radii: lexicographically largest maximal terms give a unique maximal product contribution. Scalar extension preserves the norm. Therefore N(u)=max_beta(D^−1 log|a_beta|+D^−1 sum beta_i wi), with rational floor d lambda. Polynomial degree bounds express each base generator g_j in the source generators and give u>=eta_j log|g_j compose pi|−M_j. Adding the dominated trace branches d eta_j log|g_j|−dM_j supplies the exact base-algebra generator condition. Supplied decreasing sequences trace termwise; generic finiteness of their limit is separate. Dini is used only for finite continuous limits.

For finite integral Y->S with S an affine open of A^n over the retained k, generic field-norm coefficients extend because they are integral over normal A[T] and lie in K[T]. Normalize a line preimage through the H(s)-rational lift, generically in an etale open. Height bounds and finiteness make its components curves, and normalization gives smooth finite-flat curves of total degree d. Radial equality for actual global FS tests gives the same weighted sums for every line/open. Differences of actual FS functions form a rational lattice, contain constants and separate the finite analytic fiber by truncated log norms with dominated generator branches. Their finite-set closure contains every function, so each slicing weight is fixed. At nonflat fibers these are normalized slicing weights, not necessarily dimensions of the original nonflat fiber algebra.

For a weak input choose the line after shrinking the open where its proper birational witness is an isomorphism. Properness extends each generic lift across the smooth normalized curve DVRs. The curve theorem then identifies a previously constructed globally regularizable open-trace extension with the fixed weighted trace everywhere, including minus-infinity cases. The weights were fixed before this input-specific line choice. This repairs the boundary equality required in Wu6.12 Step3, but does not construct that preceding trace extension or smooth weak upper-growth base. The cusp-product example still produces nondiscrete H(s) internally in the original projective unibranch domain; no stronger arbitrary-H(s) affine regularization theorem is inferred.

notes.summary: Ample models supply positive divisorial atoms without a Dirac equation. Algebraic collars, global FS entropy supports and nonnormal pole-order localization have direct constructions; higher-dimensional local BT and analytic-piece gluing remain gates.
notes.detailedSummary: Using n1’s genuine operator, BJ2.12/2.33 place a bounded ample model potential with positive actual mass at each source-convention divisorial point. Local domination follows only with local mass/comparison/determination antecedents. An explicit rational lattice collar formula works for global algebraic FS inputs, not arbitrary analytic PL. The calibrated corner sign is derived under finite refined harmonic-chart assumptions; general rational-domain representation and CLD strictness remain unresolved. Direct simplex/series/real-slope approximations meet actual FS generators and floors. Pole bounds use normalization and an f-power conductor. The z-square trace example proves that one gamma needs localization; gamma=1 is handled separately.
notes.text:
Using n1's genuine global operator, a new unconditional model-atom proof replaces a Dirac-equation premise. BJ2.12 realizes each source-convention divisorial x as a Rees valuation of a flag ideal on a configuration closed integrally in its prescribed generic fiber. BJ2.33 puts an ample test bundle L_model+epsilon D on this same model. On its central component E, (L_model|E)^n>0 and b_E>0, so the genuine raw weight b_E(L_model|E)^n is positive at x. The resulting potential is bounded and genuine globally psh, also for nonnormal X. This uses neither EP nor equation surjectivity. Source divisorial points are rationally scaled; no atom at every arbitrary real scaled point is asserted.

If bounded local potentials have genuine compatible mixed positive measures, exact mass V, comparison and divisorial determination, translate this test b below phi and set phi_t=(1−t)phi+t b. Under phi<=psi MA(psi)-a.e., comparison gives full MA(phi_t) mass to {phi_t<psi}; mixed positivity gives an atom >=t^n MA(b) at x. Therefore phi_t(x)<psi(x), and t->0 plus divisorial determination gives domination. These local hypotheses are not supplied by the atom itself. With them, known smooth EP and contact orthogonality would globalize bounded local potentials using a decreasing directed net of continuous majorants on compact Hausdorff analytification. A sequence of majorants is not assumed over uncountable k.

For global algebraic affine FS input a=max(lambda,q_j log|f_j|+A_j), write f_j=F_j/s0^d_j on an embedding compactification with proper exhaustion g=−log||s0||_theta>=0. If a−cg<=C on R<=g<=R+1, set G=min(g,R+1), H_j=max(log||F_j||_(d_j theta),−M_j). Choose rational clipping thresholds so −q_j M_j+(q_j d_j−c)G+A_j<=C on [0,R+1]. Clipped section norms are differences of actual basepoint-free FS metrics. BJ's rational PL space is a vector lattice, whereas its real span need not be. Set A*=max(C,lambda−cG,{q_jH_j+(q_jd_j−c)G+A_j}), choose rational K>0 with C+K>=sup A*, and F*=min(A*,C+K(R+1−G)). For g<=R the cap is inactive; on the shell A*=C; for g>=R+1, including the entire divisor, the cap is C. Thus the collar is genuinely algebraic model PL, without identifying arbitrary analytic PL with it.

These explicit local maxima have positive curvature. Flag-ideal generators show their metric over k((t)) equals pullback at every analytic point. CLD18.8.6 preserves positivity and18.8.4 applied to each residual central curve gives nonnegative degree; the represented model is nef and enters genuine PSH by the n1 model criterion. A common compact shell works for an entire tail of an already supplied decreasing global FS sequence: nested closed superlevel sets, not Dini to a singular limit, produce the collar. Genuine decreasing closure and complete-system restriction then give the legitimate already-regularizable extension. Polynomial Hartogs coefficients max_{j,i>=1}(log|f_j,i|−c_j)/i have this algebraic form when the Hartogs domain is already Runge. Adding epsilon_r g−r supplies generators and a floor. This proves no arbitrary weak-input domain is Runge.

The entropy simplex dual of chi(x)=a^−1 log(1+sum exp(a x_i)) has rational finite face-respecting polyhedral approximants with uniform error on the whole extended tropical space, including all zero-coordinate faces. Rational intercepts and vertex branches retain the floor and original generators. Error shifts make the approximants decreasing. Positive rational series use upper partial sums plus an exhaustion tail. For a real support C+sum alpha_i log|f_i|, choose log|f_i|<=d_i v, rational q_i,m increasing to alpha_i>0, B_m decreasing from above to sum d_i alpha_i, and C_m decreasing to C. Set b_m=B_m−sum d_i q_i,m>0. Then max(C_m+sum q_i,m log|f_i|+b_m v,epsilon_m v−m) decreases globally, including poles, and retains generator/floor branches. Relative entropy and compact gap sublevels prove strict separation outside every contact neighborhood. No singular envelope is used in these actual global FS supporting constructions.

For localization in an integral nonnormal affine R, suppose a log|h|+b<=max(u,−c log|f|)+O(1), h in R_f, and |log|f||<=M on L union {x}, with x in the original R-polynomial hull. Divisorial rays on the finite normalization force a max(−ord_D h,0)<=c ord_D f. For q/p>c/a, z=h^p f^q is integral over R and lies in R_f. One f^N kills R[z]/R, so z^ell f^N belongs to R for every ell. Applying the original hull inequality and letting ell->infinity, then q/p decrease to c/a, gives a log|h(x)|+b<=sup_L(a log|h|+b)+2cM, including zero and minus-infinity endpoints. This repairs false denominator counting for f=z^2,g=z. The full regularizable maximum principle still needs controlled approximants.

Under a finite harmonic chart refined by test coordinates, Green's formula gives corner coefficient sum_sigma w_sigma partial_(inward transverse) b. Subtract a harmonic contact support; tangential derivatives cancel and all transverse derivatives are nonnegative. Harmonic balancing removes the support. The sign agrees with the positive outgoing-slope Laplacian of |x|. Strongly positive facet tests have nonnegative density, and collapsed facets vanish only in the refined test chart. Applying this to every relative-image PL input still needs finite rational-domain representation. CLD17.8.4 is strict integer PL, while18.8.8 prints integer PL and cites it; this distinction is left explicit. The narrower GM route requires a proper scheme over nontrivial k((t)), rational constants cleared after tensoring, then residual nefness and BJ's smooth-only4.19. CLD8.7.2 cannot handle a merely decreasing bounded discontinuous limit.

The common representation bookkeeping is verified: with theta=omega+ddc p, a negative FS floor, h=A v+M+1, Psi=max(u−h,0), one needs Phi=Psi/A+p and G=v−p+(M+1)/A, so Phi+G=u/A. Once genuine common representations exist, BJ weighted decreasing continuity constructs local products and overlaps. Intrinsic local products, partition/integration-by-parts, exact mass and comparison are not all reconstructed here. Nor is arbitrary Rossi/split analytic-piece gluing covered by the algebraic collar. In the z->z^2 example a split-piece indicator has continuous trace two on a disk about zero and one on a disjoint disk about one; fiber dimensions remain included when unsplit. Thus gamma must be localized. If gamma=1 there is no other positive weight in that piece and no division by gamma−1. These repairs do not establish the complete Runge induction.

notes.text:
Exact disposition: the original P16.1 target and completion criteria are unchanged and remain unproved. Retain every reduced irreducible geometrically unibranch projective variety over every algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field, in every dimension, and every ample line bundle. n1 also supplies the genuine global partial theory for ample real numerical Cartier classes. n2 closes the relative-support curve positivity and radial trace equality obligation, with the preceding open-trace extension still an antecedent. n3 supplies model atoms and algebraic inputs, and records the remaining local gates. No unrelated valuation, characteristic, nonample, nonprojective or analytic equation axis is inferred.

Concrete gaps are recorded in the exact five-key status.json and the paper: (1) a complete higher-dimensional finite rational-domain representation and calibrated chart application for the whole corrected local class, with the strict/nonstrict source distinction resolved; (2) complete smooth bounded-local mixed products, partition/integration-by-parts, exact mass/comparison and genuine common representation, followed by smooth weak and controlled principal-open extension; (3) Rossi arbitrary analytic-neighborhood and split analytic-piece gluing and the full local-projection/Hartogs/Runge induction; (4) the countable rational singular envelope base, hence actual singular EP, arbitrary-cardinality/real-class passage, unconditional variational existence and onto normalization. Positivity of individual PL currents or the radial boundary equality cannot construct these antecedents.

Normalization q of a geometrically unibranch X is finite birational degree one, with singleton geometric fibers and unchanged residue fields in characteristic zero. Its analytification is a homeomorphism. Unconditionally E(q*phi)=E(phi), volume is unchanged and q_* genuine mixed MA(q*phi_i)=genuine mixed MA(phi_i), by projection formula and decreasing pairings. Onto PSH separately requires BJ5.13's approaching larger classes with EP. Onto E1, equal dual energies and full operator/target correspondence then follow, but are not proved here without that antecedent. The conditional cardinality argument descends finite data to countable algebraically closed subfields, preserves relative closure by vertical R1/S2 and regular extension, checks components/multiplicities/intersection degrees, and uses actual mixed pushforward, contact orthogonality and BJ global domination. Real classes require genuine class closure from above. Neither passage supplies the missing base.

The nodal obstruction is unconditional. Let C be a rational irreducible projective nodal curve, with normalization P1 and distinct node preimages p1,p2; put d=deg L>0 and v=ord_p1. The downstairs delta_v has finite dual energy. Blow up P1 times A1 at (p1,0). The model p*(q*L)+d X0−d E has central degrees 0,d and multiplicities one, so it is nef and has genuine raw measure d delta_v. Its bounded potential is d max(1−s,0) on the p1 ray and d on other rays, with node-preimage endpoint values 0,d. A downstairs E1 solution would pull up with the same target by genuine pushforward, positivity, fixed mass and the singleton lift of the function-field valuation. Upstairs uniqueness forces this potential plus a constant, while a downstairs pullback must have equal endpoint values. Contradiction. This is an actual finite-energy nonsolvability obstruction outside unibranchness.
